name: Bahrain

income_tax.summary: Bahrain has no personal income tax (PwC, reviewed 26 Jul 2026). Employees in Bahrain contribute to the Social Insurance Organisation: expatriates pay 1% (employer 3%), Bahrainis 8% (employer 18%). Income paid outside Bahrain is not subject to Bahraini tax or social insurance rules.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed contributions are not covered by the PwC page; none are assumed. Foreign-paid income is outside the Bahraini social insurance rules.

open_questions: PwC other-taxes page re-opened 2026-10-15: expatriate employees 1% (employer 3%), Bahrainis 8% (employer 18%). It gives no contribution ceiling, no unemployment-insurance split and no self-employed rate; self-employed 0% is an unsourced assumption (confidence kept at medium).

residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: no visa-free right to work. Skilled employees obtain a work permit and residence through a Bahraini employer. One news article (May 2026, not opened) mentions expanded digital-residency pathways, but no nomad visa terms were verified.
open_questions: Whether Bahrain has a remote-work or digital-residency visa, and on what terms, was not verified from an official source.
